newsitem.title: BELARUS: Police use teargas, make arrests at Belarus protest.
newsitem.headline: Police use teargas, make arrests at Belarus protest.

text.p: Police used tear gas and made several arrests after at least 3,000 protesters demonstrated against President Alexander Lukashenko in Minsk on Friday, waving flags, blowing whistles and shouting "Down with Luka."
A reporter at the scene saw police arrest between 10 and 20 people and an Estonian woman journalist was taken to hospital with an eye injury after exposure to tear gas.
A police spokesman said he could give no figures on arrests, put at 40 by the Belarussian National Front which helped organise the protest.
The mostly young crowd handed in petitions to the embassies of France, Britain, Italy and Germany and moved on towards the U.S. embassy. Special OMON forces blocked off the president's building.
The protesters waved banners reading "Belarus into Europe" and shouted slogans against Lukashenko and his pro-Russian policies.
Nationalists in the republic of 10 million people want Belarus to look west towards Europe rather than east towards Russia.

They find solace in criticism from European institutions of Lukashenko's authoritarian approach, especially since a controversial referendum in November authorised him to take broad powers and rewrite the constitution.

The Council of Europe said the new constitution failed to meet minimum human rights standards, while Europe's top security body, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, has repeatedly called on Belarus to restore democracy.
